absent: Lower-level probe constructor and destructor behavior for kernel and user probes, including validation beyond type, privilege and branch-stack checks.
Internals of the subscriber match predicate, software-event delivery, trace-buffer refresh and recursion-context management.
Blocking program setter, handler release and detach behavior distinguishing tracing versus non-tracing events.
Address-filter virtual-area adjustment logic and range semantics for file-backed versus direct filters.
Remainder of unit teardown beyond the possible-processor loop header, and behavior of the named free helper without visible body.
Online mask maintenance and scope assignment for units.
Overflow, exclusion and idle-task determination logic used by timer and breakpoint paths.

findings.text: Tracepoint delivery receives an event type, count, raw record pointer with size, register context, subscriber list, recursion handle and optional target task. It refreshes the shared trace buffer for the type, then visits each subscriber under read-copy-update protection; for subscribers accepted by the match predicate it reinitializes a reused on-stack sample, attaches the raw fragment and forwards through the software-event path. When a distinct target task is supplied it additionally walks that task pinned and flexible groups for the calling processor, then always releases the recursion handle.

Tracepoint delivery runs with preemption disabled and breakpoint delivery runs with interrupts disabled, each enforced by an entry assertion. The software timer callback obtains registers from interrupt context and skips excluded events, including idle-task exclusion when configured.

Delivery to a foreign task holds a read-side section while dereferencing the target context pointer, then holds that context raw spinlock across the group walk. A missing context ends the attempt without locking, and the read-side section is always released.

Per-event filtering for foreign-task delivery requires the event configuration to equal the record type and rejects events requesting synchronous trap delivery. Only survivors reach the match predicate with fresh sample initialization.
Probe configuration reserves bit 0 as return-probe marker. User-probe reference-counter offset occupies the top 32 bits of a 64-bit configuration, with shift equal to 64 minus 32.

The kernel-probe unit uses software task context and routes lifetime operations to trace add and delete plus software start, stop and read. It exposes one format attribute for the return-probe flag and initializes through a dedicated routine that installs dedicated teardown on success.

Kernel-probe initialization rejects mismatched types, requires performance-monitoring capability, refuses branch-stack sampling, extracts the return-probe flag from configuration for the lower-level constructor and propagates constructor errors.
The user-probe unit mirrors kernel-probe lifetime routing under software task context but exposes two format attributes, one for the return-probe flag and one for the reference-counter offset.

User-probe initialization rejects mismatched types, requires administrator privilege, refuses branch-stack sampling, decodes the return-probe flag from the low bit and the reference-counter offset from the high bits for the lower-level constructor, and installs teardown on success.

Tracepoint registration has two build configurations. One registers tracepoint, kernel-probe and user-probe units under the names tracepoint, kprobe and uprobe with fixed type for the first and dynamic types for the probes behind feature guards. The other is an empty no-operation.

Blocking event program attachment locks the event context around the underlying setter and returns its status, while the alternate build always reports missing support. Release does nothing when no program is attached, otherwise routes non-tracing events to handler release and tracing events to detach. The alternate build release does nothing.
Breakpoint delivery initializes a sample with the breakpoint address, then forwards a single count only when hardware is not marked stopped and the exclusion predicate accepts the register context.

Address-filter teardown assumes no concurrency and splices the list away only when non-empty. File-backed application walks all virtual areas of a memory descriptor, skipping areas without a file, and stops at the first adjustment reporting completion.

Range application skips tombstone tasks, acquires a memory reference with read lock only when file filters exist, then under interrupt-safe filter lock rebuilds each range either by clearing plus adjusting against mapped files or by copying direct offset and size, bumps the generation counter, releases locks and references, and unconditionally restarts the event.

Address-filter text parsing distinguishes three actions plus a none value encoded as negative one, four sources and three parser states starting at zero. The vocabulary maps the words filter, start and stop to actions and four numeric patterns with optional file suffix to sources.

The software timer callback stops when the event is inactive or marked stopped, otherwise reads the counter, samples with last period and interrupt registers subject to exclusion and idle checks, advances the timer by the sample period clamped to a minimum of 10000 nanoseconds and continues unless overflow handling requests termination.

Timer start applies only to sampling events, consuming a saved remainder or the clamped sample period with negative remainders replaced by the minimum. Cancel preserves remaining time and uses a non-blocking attempt to avoid deadlock with the callback, relying on the stopped flag for termination. Destroy cancels unconditionally. Initialization sets up a monotonic relative hard timer and converts frequency mode into a fixed period while clearing frequency mode.

Processor-clock events accumulate elapsed local time via atomic exchange and add, clear hardware state on start while seeding the previous stamp and arming the timer, set the stopped flag on stop while disarming and optionally updating, support add with optional start plus user-page refresh, delete as updating stop, read as update, and accept only their own type with processor-clock configuration while rejecting branch sampling.

Task-clock events mirror processor-clock lifecycle but seed and update from task time, with reads composing current time from context stamp plus elapsed performance clock. Initialization enforces its own type with task-clock configuration and rejects branch sampling.

Default transaction handlers provide empty operations with zero or success returns. Generic start records per-processor flags and disables the unit only for add-only transactions, while commit and cancel clear flags and re-enable only in that same case. The default event index is zero.

Unit devices expose type, multiplex interval, address-filter count and processor mask attributes. The filter-count file hides when the unit declares none and the mask hides when scope is none, otherwise original modes apply.

Multiplex-interval display reports the unit millisecond setting. Updates parse an integer, reject values below one and no-change writes, then under a dedicated mutex and processor-set read lock rewrite the unit setting and every online processor context interval followed by a restart signal per processor.

Scope resolution maps core, die, cluster, package and system-wide scopes to respective online masks and yields nothing otherwise. The mask file prints the resolved mask or empty output when unresolved.

Device allocation creates and initializes a device bound to the bus named event_source with driver data, parent and release destructor, assigns the unit name, adds the device and applies attribute updates, unwinding through delete and release on failure. Release frees the device object.

Unit teardown removes the filter-count file when present and deletes plus releases the device when the bus is active and the device is valid, then iterates possible processors. Identifier exchange validates the old mapping before replacing and warns if the replaced value differs. A static registry backs unit identifiers, with two dedicated lock classes distinguishing context mutex and spinlock.

Processor-clock and task-clock units share software task context, advertise absence of non-maskable-interrupt support with a null device, and route all lifecycle operations to their respective clock handlers.

Cancelling the sampling timer from within its own callback would deadlock with a blocking cancel. The implementation avoids this with a non-blocking attempt plus a stopped flag honored by the callback on its next run.

Reusing one on-stack sample across multiple deliveries risks carrying flags that suppress preparation for later events. The code reinitializes the sample before each delivery to prevent skipped setup.

Filter application may observe a tombstone task or a task without memory, in which case it either returns early or proceeds directly to event restart without touching ranges, avoiding use of invalid memory references.
